findings.title: Mocked verify-candidate can green while live Actions topology differs
findings.why_it_matters: Merge-blocking validate proves candidate verification only against a fixed nine-job fixture, not the live Actions jobs/attestation APIs. A hosted release run whose reusable-workflow job flattening, naming, or pagination differs can fail promotion verification after CI is already green, or briefly appear trusted if expectations were wrong in the opposite direction.

findings.why_it_matter: The build job checks out github.sha while the reusable CI job builds inputs.source_sha. Trust rests entirely on the identity job’s environment guard; any future workflow edit that weakens or bypasses identity while keeping build would compile a different commit than CI gated.

findings.first_evidence: scripts/candidate.sh:117-120: artifact_id and artifact_digest read from artifacts API only
findings.suggested_fix: In verify(), download the candidate artifact by artifact_id into a fresh temp tree (same gh deadline bounds), hash the ZIP or unpacked file set, and require equality with artifact_api_digest or a manifest of member digests before attesting CANDIDATE_DIR contents.
findings.title: Local candidate bytes not bound to artifact transport digest
findings.why_it_matters: Maintainer verification cryptographically attests files in CANDIDATE_DIR and records artifact_api_digest from the API, but never downloads the Actions artifact ZIP and compares its hash to that digest. A hand-assembled or partially extracted directory that still passes per-file attestation checks can be accepted without proving it is the same transport payload GitHub stored.

scripts/promote.sh:71: CANDIDATE_VERIFICATION_DIR="$output/verification" make verify-candidate reuses nested output tree
findings.suggested_fix: Treat an existing gh-deadline binary as reusable when its digest matches a freshly built artifact, or always build into a unique subdirectory per verify attempt while keeping mkdir collision semantics for receipts.
findings.title: gh_deadline_setup fails when driver already exists
findings.why_it_matters: If gh-deadline.exe is left in the verification output directory from a partial run, a subsequent verify or promote retry in that directory fails setup before any readback, leaving operators to interpret a tooling collision instead of resuming bounded reconciliation.

residual_risks: Candidate job-count and name matching assumes GitHub continues to flatten reusable-workflow matrix jobs into the parent run with ci / prefixes; API or naming changes fail closed but require script updates before any release can verify.
Native performance and terminal acceptance remain hash-bound local artifacts; hosted/native publication proof is explicitly pending per feature scope, so CI green does not close release acceptance.
artifact_api_digest is retained for audit but promotion paths never reconcile it against a downloaded ZIP, leaving transport integrity to operator procedure.
testing_gaps: No automated test exercises verify-candidate against a recorded real Actions jobs.json/artifacts.json capture from a completed release run (only the synthetic nine-job fixture).
No test downloads a release-workflow artifact ZIP and asserts member digests match artifact_api_digest plus local CANDIDATE_DIR attestation subjects.
